policy_title: Prepare for renegotiations on the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement
stated: Reform UK will prepare for renegotiations on the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement, stating that a 'level playing field' is holding Britain back.

source.quote: Prepare for Renegotiations on the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement A so-called EU ‘level playing field’ is holding us back.

bearing_set.reason: Renegotiating the TCA's level-playing-field provisions (including tariff schedules and regulatory alignment) would materially affect the cost of traded goods — especially food — and the broader inflation basket for UK households.

The TCA's level-playing-field chapter explicitly constrains the UK from weakening labour rights and standards to gain competitive advantage; removing those constraints bears directly on employment rights, pay floors, and job quality.

The TCA's level playing field explicitly covers environmental and climate standards; removing or weakening those constraints would directly affect the UK's emissions trajectory, air-quality, and water-quality indicators.

Renegotiating the TCA with the UK's largest trading partner (≈40 % of UK trade) directly affects productivity, business investment, and real living standards — both upside (regulatory freedom/industrial policy) and downside (risk of EU retaliation and tighter market access).

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the trade-prosperity channel (O13), the labour-standards channel (O4), and the environmental-standards channel (O6) all flow directly from removing level-playing-field constraints — the policy's stated purpose. Food-price effects via EU retaliation are real but sufficiently subsumed in the O13 trade-disruption verdict at this stage of the pipeline.
